# Yazi configuration (tested with v0.3.3+, syntax updated for v25.12.29+)

[manager]

# -----------------------
# Image DECODE bound. yazi's built-in image previewer decodes an image with the
# `image` crate's Limits capped at [tasks].image_bound (default [10000, 10000] px)
# BEFORE downscaling to the small [preview] max_width/max_height (600x900) — so a
# wide time-series/plot PNG or a huge screenshot (>10000 px on a side) is rejected
# outright with "Image size exceeds limit" in the preview pane. Raise the bound so
# large images preview; image_alloc (512 MB, kept from the preset via deep-merge)
# stays the real memory guard. Run `yazi --clear-cache` after changing (cached
# failed previews persist). See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.

[tasks]
image_bound = [ 30000, 30000 ]

# -----------------------
# Previewers — three families this repo wires explicitly, via yazi plugins
# auto-installed by `ya pkg install` on chezmoi apply (lockfile:
# dot_config/yazi/package.toml; installer:
# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl).
# NOTE: images / PDF / video / SVG / standard archives are handled by yazi's
# BUILT-IN previewers (not wired here); those shell out to chafa/poppler/7zip/
# resvg — plus ffmpeg/imagemagick when installMediaTools — installed by the
# devtools/media_tools ansible roles. See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
#
#   1. DATA FILES → duckdb.yazi (run = "duckdb"): csv/tsv/parquet/xlsx/db/duckdb.
#      Native DuckDB table view; K toggles SUMMARIZE, H/L scroll columns (see
#      keymap.toml); init.lua runs the REQUIRED `require("duckdb"):setup{}`. Needs
#      the `duckdb` CLI (devtools role). Two gaps filled via piper below:
#        - .feather/.arrow  → DuckDB has no Arrow-IPC reader → visidata `fixed`.
#        - .sqlite/.sqlite3 → not in the plugin's extension_map → duckdb table list
#          (plain `.db` IS handled by the plugin: DuckDB auto-attaches SQLite).
#   2. OFFICE DOCS → piper.yazi piping the in-house `view-office` dispatcher
#      (doxx / markitdown / LibreOffice).
#   3. CONTAINERS / e-books yazi's built-ins skip → piper: .epub (pandoc text),
#      Kindle .mobi/.azw/.azw3/.fb2 (view-ebook → calibre metadata), and .dmg
#      (7-Zip listing) — none of these mimes are in the built-in archive set.
#
# CONTRACTS / gotchas:
#   - view-office entries must stay in sync with view-office's --preview/--width
#     interface (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office).
#   - piper passes $w=width, $h=height, $1=file path and runs the string via
#     `sh -c` (pipes/redirects work). piper renders any STDERR as an error, so the
#     visidata/duckdb/pandoc/7z fallbacks MUST keep `2>/dev/null`.
#   - .xlsx PREVIEW is owned by duckdb.yazi here (first xlsx preview per machine
#     fetches DuckDB's `spatial` ext → needs network once). The `view-office` CLI
#     still previews xlsx via markitdown; only yazi's previewer moved.
# See docs/tools/data-viewers.md, docs/tools/office-viewers.md, docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
# -----------------------
[plugin]
prepend_previewers = [
  # --- Data files → duckdb.yazi (native table view) ---
  { url = "*.csv", run = "duckdb" },
  { url = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb" },
  { url = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb" },
  { url = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb" },
  { url = "*.db", run = "duckdb" },
  { url = "*.duckdb", run = "duckdb" },
  # --- Feather / Arrow → visidata `fixed` table (no DuckDB Arrow-IPC reader) ---
  { url = "*.feather", run = 'piper -- vd -b -f arrow "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
  { url = "*.arrow", run = 'piper -- vd -b -f arrow "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
  # --- SQLite by .sqlite/.sqlite3 name → duckdb table listing (plugin only maps .db) ---
  { url = "*.sqlite", run = 'piper -- duckdb -readonly "$1" -box -c "SELECT table_name, column_count AS cols FROM duckdb_tables() ORDER BY table_name" 2>/dev/null' },
  { url = "*.sqlite3", run = 'piper -- duckdb -readonly "$1" -box -c "SELECT table_name, column_count AS cols FROM duckdb_tables() ORDER BY table_name" 2>/dev/null' },

  # --- Office / OpenDocument → view-office (piper). .xlsx handled by duckdb above. ---
  { url = "*.docx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.pptx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  # Legacy binary + OpenDocument (LibreOffice converts → re-dispatches)
  { url = "*.doc", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.xls", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.ppt", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.odt", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.ods", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.odp", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.rtf", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },

  # --- Containers yazi's built-in previewers skip → piper ---
  # EPUB (application/epub+zip) → pandoc plain text; .dmg (application/x-apple-
  # diskimage) → 7-Zip content listing. Both mimes are absent from yazi's built-in
  # archive set, so without these they show only file-type classification.
  # (.zip/.tar.*/.7z/.rar and zip-based .apk/.jar/.whl/.xpi ARE handled free by the
  # built-in archive previewer once 7-Zip is installed — no rule needed.)
  # 2>/dev/null is load-bearing (piper renders stderr as an error preview);
  # 7zz→macOS `sevenzip`, 7z→Linux `p7zip-full`. pandoc is a devtools-role tool.
  { url = "*.epub", run = 'piper -- pandoc -f epub -t plain "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
  # Kindle / calibre e-books (pandoc can't read these) → view-ebook: calibre
  # ebook-meta metadata (title/author/description). Best-effort — no preview if
  # calibre is absent. See the installCalibre prompt + docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
  { url = "*.mobi", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.azw", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.azw3", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.fb2", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  { url = "*.dmg", run = 'piper -- ( 7zz l "$1" 2>/dev/null || 7z l "$1" 2>/dev/null ) | head -n 200' },
]

# duckdb.yazi builds parquet scroll-caches in a preload step — it needs matching
# preloader rules for the tabular formats (NOT .db/.duckdb, which are not
# pre-cached; NOT the piper fallbacks). See the plugin README.
prepend_preloaders = [
  { url = "*.csv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
  { url = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
  { url = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
  { url = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
]
```

-- ~/.config/yazi/init.lua
-- Yazi Lua init — runs once at startup. Managed by chezmoi
-- (source: dot_config/yazi/init.lua). Edits to ~/.config/yazi/init.lua are
-- reverted on next `chezmoi apply` — change the source instead.
--
-- Documentation: https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/overview

-- duckdb.yazi — DuckDB-powered table previewer for data files
-- (csv/tsv/parquet/xlsx/db/duckdb). This setup() call is REQUIRED: it registers
-- the plugin's previewer/preloader; without it the `run = "duckdb"` rules in
-- yazi.toml never activate.
--
--   mode = "standard"   → hover shows actual data rows (press K at top-of-file
--                         to toggle to DuckDB's SUMMARIZE view: min/max/counts).
--                         The plugin default is "summarized"; we prefer showing
--                         rows first for a quick "what's in this file" glance.

```text
#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild bat theme cache when the managed Tokyo Night theme changes
# bat theme: {{ include "dot_config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme" | sha256sum }}

set -e
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
fi
{{ else -}}
if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
fi
{{ end -}}

info() { echo -e "\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m $1"; }
success() { echo -e "\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m $1"; }
warn() { echo -e "\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m $1"; }

if ! command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    info "bat not installed; skipping theme cache rebuild"
    exit 0
fi

THEME_FILE="$(bat --config-dir)/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme"
if [[ ! -f "$THEME_FILE" ]]; then
    warn "bat theme file not found: $THEME_FILE"
    exit 0
fi

info "Rebuilding bat theme cache"
bat cache --build >/dev/null

if command -v delta >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "bat cache is incompatible with delta; clearing cache so git pager keeps working"
    bat cache --clear >/dev/null
    exit 0
fi

success "bat theme cache rebuilt"
```
</details></tool-use>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Delta handles the cache correctly with version 0.19.2 and bat 0.26.1, so that issue is resolved. Now I'm looking at the pitfall documentation to understand what the original problem was — it's about empty stdin causing huge memory allocation, and the test case pipes empty input to delta to check for this behavior.

The guard clears the cache if delta fails, which happens when bat's cache is incompatible. But here's the real problem: the `run_onchange` script only re-runs when the theme file hash changes. If the cache gets cleared for any reason — whether the guard triggered it, the user ran `bat cache --clear`, a bat upgrade invalidated it, or `~/.cache` was wiped — the script never rebuilds the cache. Since the theme file hasn't changed, the script stays dormant and the BAT_THEME warning persists.

The better solution is to make the script self-healing: check if `bat --list-themes` actually contains the theme, and rebuild if it's missing. Either run it on every apply instead of just on changes, or keep the hash-gating but add a fallback check. I could use mtime comparisons as a pure stat check — no bat invocation needed. The guard would verify that bat is installed, the theme file exists, and the cache file is newer than both the theme and the bat binary itself. This handles cache clears and bat upgrades cleanly. But there's a wrinkle: if delta clears the cache due to incompatibility, the next apply would fail the fast path and rebuild, triggering delta's test again, which clears the cache again — creating a noisy rebuild loop every apply. I need to think through how to break that cycle. The warning shows up whenever bat runs with BAT_THEME set and the cache is missing, so it could come from direct bat invocations, fzf previews, or other preview workflows. I should check yazi's theme.toml to see if it has its own syntect theme configuration for code previews, and then investigate where bat is actually being called in these different contexts.

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>

```text
# git-delta crashes on empty stdin with huge allocation

**Symptoms** (grep this section): `delta` exits with `memory allocation of 1970324836974592 bytes failed`; zsh reports `IOT instruction (core dumped)  delta`; `delta --version` prints normally; `printf '' | delta` crashes; `BAT_THEME=` can panic with `something is very wrong if the default theme is missing`.
**First seen**: 2026-05
**Affects**: `git-delta 0.18.2` / `0.19.2` on Linux when `~/.cache/bat/*.bin` was built by an incompatible `bat` version.
**Status**: fixed in repo setup by preferring Linuxbrew `bat` when available, clearing incompatible bat cache, and using a stdin health check for delta.

## Symptom

Running `delta` directly, or invoking Git commands that use `core.pager = delta`, aborts:

```text
memory allocation of 1970324836974592 bytes failed
[1]    2783953 IOT instruction (core dumped)  delta
```

The version check is misleadingly healthy:

```sh
delta --version
# delta 0.18.2
```

But processing even empty stdin reproduces it:

```sh
printf '' | delta
# memory allocation of 1970324836974592 bytes failed
```

With `BAT_THEME` unset, the same binary may show the missing embedded-theme panic instead:

```text
thread 'main' panicked at .../bat-0.24.0/src/assets.rs:252:22:
something is very wrong if the default theme is missing
```

## Root Cause

`delta` can start and report its version, but fails on the rendering path that loads bat syntax/theme assets. The backtrace points at `bat::assets::lazy_theme_set::LazyTheme::deserialize` reading bincode cache data.

The trigger observed here was `~/.cache/bat/themes.bin` / `syntaxes.bin` built by system `bat 0.19.0`, while `delta 0.19.2` embedded `bat 0.26.1`. Clearing the cache makes delta fall back to its embedded defaults and stops the crash. This is not caused by this repo's `core.pager = delta` setting.

This repo previously rebuilt the bat cache after installing the managed Tokyo Night theme, but did not verify whether that cache was compatible with delta.

## Workaround

Immediate recovery is to clear the bat cache:

```sh
bat cache --clear
```

If `BAT_THEME=tokyonight_night` is set, delta may warn that the theme is unknown after clearing the cache; that warning is preferable to the crash. To restore the custom theme safely on a Linuxbrew host, install a newer brew `bat`, rebuild the cache with that binary, and re-test delta:

```sh
brew install bat git-delta
rehash 2>/dev/null || hash -r
bat cache --build
bat --list-themes | rg 'tokyonight_night'
printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never
```

`chezmoi apply` is enough only after the active `bat` is compatible with the active `delta`. If apply rebuilds the cache with old apt `bat 0.19.0`, the repo's guard will clear the incompatible cache so delta works, but `delta` will fall back to its default theme.

## Prevention

The `devtools` role validates delta with:

```sh
printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never
```

When Linuxbrew exists on Debian/Ubuntu, the `devtools` role installs brew `bat` so the bat cache is generated by a version compatible with brew `delta`. The bat theme run-script rebuilds the bat cache, then immediately runs the same delta health check. If delta fails, the script clears the bat cache so the Git pager keeps working.

On Debian/Ubuntu x86_64, the role installs upstream GNU artifacts:

```text
git-delta_<version>_amd64.deb
delta-<version>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
```

Do not regress the health check to `delta --version` only; that misses this failure mode.

## Related

- `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` git-delta install block
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl`
```
</details></tool-use>

--- @since 26.1.22

local M = {}

local function fail(job, s) ya.preview_widget(job, ui.Text.parse(s):area(job.area):wrap(ui.Wrap.YES)) end

function M:peek(job)
	local child, err = Command("sh")
		:arg({ "-c", job.args[1], "sh", tostring(job.file.path) })
		:env("w", job.area.w)
		:env("h", job.area.h)
		:env("t", rt.term.light and "light" or "dark")
		:env("CYGWIN", "noupcaseenv")
		:stdout(Command.PIPED)
		:stderr(Command.PIPED)
		:spawn()

	if not child then
		return fail(job, "sh: " .. err)
	end

	local limit = job.area.h
	local i, outs, errs = 0, {}, {}
	repeat
		local next, event = child:read_line()
		if event == 1 then
			errs[#errs + 1] = next
		elseif event ~= 0 then
			break
		end

		i = i + 1
		if i > job.skip then
			outs[#outs + 1] = next
		end
	until i >= job.skip + limit

	child:start_kill()
	if #errs > 0 then
		fail(job, table.concat(errs, ""))
	elseif job.skip > 0 and i < job.skip + limit then
		ya.emit("peek", { math.max(0, i - limit), only_if = job.file.url, upper_bound = true })
	else
		ya.preview_widget(job, M.format(job, outs))
	end
end

function M:seek(job) require("code"):seek(job) end

function M.format(job, lines)
	local format = job.args.format
	if format ~= "url" then
		local s = table.concat(lines, ""):gsub("\t", string.rep(" ", rt.preview.tab_size))
		return ui.Text.parse(s):area(job.area)
	end

	for i = 1, #lines do
		lines[i] = lines[i]:gsub("[\r\n]+$", "")

		local icon
		if th.icon then
			icon = th.icon:match(File {
				url = Url(lines[i]),
				cha = Cha { mode = tonumber(lines[i]:sub(-1) == "/" and "40700" or "100644", 8) },
			})

			icon = File({

				cha = Cha { mode = tonumber(lines[i]:sub(-1) == "/" and "40700" or "100644", 8) },
			}):icon()
		end

		if icon then
			lines[i] = ui.Line { ui.Span(" " .. icon.text .. " "):style(icon.style), lines[i] }
		end
	end
	return ui.Text(lines):area(job.area)
end

return M

```text
     201 docs/tools/yazi-previews.md
# Yazi Preview Coverage

Maximize what the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager can preview on hover — **images, PDF, video,
SVG, archives, ebooks, dmg**, on top of the tabular/office stacks documented in
[data-viewers.md](data-viewers.md) and [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md).

The catch: yazi's **built-in** previewers (images / PDF / video / SVG / standard archives) are *not*
wired in `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` — yazi ships them internally and **shells out to external
binaries at runtime**. If those binaries aren't installed, the hover pane shows an error
(`failed to spawn chafa`) or bare file-type classification. So "expanding coverage" is mostly a
**tool-install** job (a few ansible-managed binaries), plus a handful of small config rules for the
container / e-book formats yazi ignores by default.

## TL;DR — coverage matrix

| File type | Preview | Powered by | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| png / jpg / webp / gif / bmp | image (or unicode-art) | yazi built-in → **chafa** to display | baseline |
| **PDF** | first page as image | yazi built-in → **poppler** (`pdftoppm`) + chafa | baseline |
| **SVG** | rendered image | yazi built-in → **resvg** + chafa | baseline |
| archives: zip / tar / gz / 7z / rar (+ zip-based apk / jar / whl / xpi) | file listing | yazi built-in → **7-Zip** | baseline |
| **dmg** | file listing | piper → **7-Zip** (`*.dmg` rule) | baseline |
| **EPUB** | text | piper → **pandoc** (`*.epub` rule) | baseline |
| **Kindle** .mobi / .azw / .azw3 / .fb2 | metadata (title/author/description) | piper → **view-ebook** → calibre `ebook-meta` | opt-in (installCalibre) |
| video: mp4 / mkv / mov … | thumbnail | yazi built-in → **ffmpeg** + chafa | media (gated) |
| HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts | image / sample | yazi built-in → **ImageMagick ≥7.1.1** + chafa | media (gated) |
| csv / tsv / parquet / xlsx / db / sqlite / feather | table | duckdb.yazi + fallbacks | plugin — see [data-viewers.md](data-viewers.md) |
| docx / **pptx** / legacy / ODF | text (image-only pptx → slide-1 thumbnail) | view-office (doxx / markitdown / chafa / LibreOffice) | plugin — see [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md) |
| txt / json / md / source | text (+ syntax) | yazi built-in / `bat` | always |

- **Baseline** tools are installed unconditionally by the `devtools` role (next to yazi).
- **Media (gated)** tools live in the `media_tools` role behind the `installMediaTools` prompt
  (default **off**; forced off on server/minimal). Video + HEIC previews work only where you opted in.

## Why images showed `failed to spawn chafa`

Every image-derived preview funnels through the same final **display** step. yazi renders png (direct),
PDF (via poppler), video (via ffmpeg), HEIC (via ImageMagick), SVG (via resvg) all *to an image*, then
hands that image to the display adapter it auto-selected. yazi picks the adapter from your terminal:
Kitty graphics protocol, iTerm2 inline, Sixel, Überzug++ (X11/Wayland), and — when none of those is
available (a non-graphics terminal, or inside tmux without passthrough) — **chafa**, its documented
*"last fallback resort"* that draws the image as Unicode/ANSI art.

So a missing `chafa` breaks **all** of png/pdf/mp4/HEIC at once, even though poppler/ffmpeg/magick are
present — they produce the image fine; nothing can display it. Installing `chafa` fixes the whole set.

### Which terminal gets crisp images vs ascii-art

chafa gives **universal ASCII/ANSI-art** previews that work everywhere — over tmux, SSH, any terminal.
For **crisp inline images**, run yazi in a terminal that speaks an image graphics protocol; yazi
auto-detects it (from `$TERM` / `$TERM_PROGRAM` / `$XDG_SESSION_TYPE`) and upgrades the adapter, no
config change. yazi's adapters, in priority order:

| Adapter | Protocol | Terminals (non-exhaustive) |
|---|---|---|
| **Kgp** | Kitty graphics protocol | **kitty**, **Ghostty** / **cmux**, WezTerm, Konsole, wayst |
| **Iip** | iTerm2 inline images | **iTerm2**, WezTerm, Warp, Rio, Tabby, VSCode (partial) |
| **Sixel** | Sixel | foot, Contour, mlterm, WezTerm, Windows Terminal, Rio, xterm (`+sixel`) |
| **X11 / Wayland** | Überzug++ overlay | any terminal on Linux X11/Wayland (needs Überzug++ installed) |
| **Chafa** | Unicode / ANSI art | **everything else** — Alacritty, macOS Terminal.app, tmux-without-passthrough, plain SSH |

- **No native protocol → chafa.** Notably **Alacritty** and **macOS Terminal.app** have *no* image
  protocol, so yazi always falls back to chafa there (this repo's [`--probe off` shim](#chafa-probe-leak)
  keeps that path clean). Ghostty / cmux / kitty / iTerm2 / WezTerm give real inline images.
- **Inside a multiplexer** the *terminal* still has to support the protocol AND the mux has to pass it
  through: tmux needs `allow-passthrough on` (set here in `dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl`) — but the
  legacy `KgpOld` variant doesn't work under tmux, and Sixel needs a `--enable-sixel` tmux build. zellij's
  image support is limited and shares the same [OSC-query leak](#chafa-probe-leak) class as the chafa bug.
- **See which adapter yazi picked**: `yazi --debug` → the `Adapter.matches` line.

If you only ever get ascii-art, that's the terminal/tmux graphics story, **not** a missing tool — chafa
is doing its job. See yazi's [image-preview docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/).

### Large images: "Image size exceeds limit" {#image-size-limit}

A big screenshot or a wide time-series / plot PNG can show **`Image size exceeds limit`** instead of a
preview. That's yazi's **decode** guard, not the terminal: yazi decodes the image with the `image`
crate bounded by `[tasks] image_bound` (default **`[10000, 10000]`** px) *before* downscaling to the
small `[preview] max_width`/`max_height` (600×900), so anything over 10000 px on a side is rejected up
front (confirmed in `yazi-adapter`: `limits.max_image_width = Some(YAZI.tasks.image_bound[0])`). This
```

```text
# Git Diff Workflow

This repo manages a small Git review stack instead of forcing a single tool to do everything:

- `delta` is the default pager for normal `git diff`, `git show`, and other CLI diff output.
- `diffnav` is a GitHub-style diff navigator with a file tree, useful when you want to move around larger patches quickly.
- `gh-dash` is the GitHub dashboard and review UI; its diff pager is configured to call `diffnav`.
- `lazygit` stays focused on repo operations inside LazyVim, with `delta` configured as its custom pager.

## Managed Config Files

This workflow is managed globally through these files:

- `~/.gitconfig` keeps `delta` as the default Git pager.
- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` sets `pager.diff: "diffnav"`.
- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` uses LazyGit's current `git.pagers` syntax with `delta`.
- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` provides the shared Tokyo Night theme used by `bat` previews.

## Why Both `delta` and `diffnav`

`delta` is still the best default for everyday Git CLI output. It is fast, readable, and already fits `git diff` and LazyGit well.

`diffnav` solves a different problem: navigating large review diffs with a file tree and a GitHub-like layout. That makes it a better fit for `gh-dash` than replacing `delta` everywhere.

## `gh-dash` + `diffnav`

`gh-dash` is installed as a `gh` extension and reads the global config at `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml`. This repo intentionally keeps that config minimal:

```yaml
pager:
  diff: "diffnav"
```

That gives `gh-dash` a better diff viewer without importing personalized sections, colors, or keybindings from other dotfiles.

Before using `gh-dash`, authenticate GitHub CLI once:

```bash
gh auth login
gh dash
```

## LazyGit + `delta`

LazyGit's current pager configuration uses `git.pagers`, not the older `git.paging` key:

```yaml
git:
  pagers:
    - colorArg: always
      pager: delta --dark --paging=never --syntax-theme base16-256 -s
```

This keeps LazyGit aligned with the existing `delta`-first CLI setup while avoiding the outdated config shape from the old issue thread.

## Fonts and Theme

Both `diffnav` and `gh-dash` look better with a Nerd Font because their interfaces rely on icon glyphs. This repo already manages Hack Nerd Font on desktop profiles.

The `bat` Tokyo Night warning is fixed by managing the upstream `tokyonight_night.tmTheme` file directly and rebuilding the bat theme cache after apply.

## References

- [diffnav](https://github.com/dlvhdr/diffnav)
- [gh-dash docs](https://www.gh-dash.dev/getting-started/)
- [LazyGit custom pagers](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/master/docs/Custom_Pagers.md)
- [bat](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat)
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
#!/bin/bash
# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs after every `chezmoi
# apply`. Detects tools whose binaries were upgraded since the last completion
# generation (binary mtime > completion file mtime → regen).
#
# `run_after_*` (not `run_onchange_after_*`): we want to detect tools that
# ansible / brew / mise / uv upgraded BETWEEN applies. Onchange would only fire
# when this script's content changes — that misses every package upgrade.
# Cost when nothing changed: ~50ms (presence checks + 28 stat calls).
#
# Tools handled (the "self-generating" set from docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md
# Section A): chezmoi, mise, uv, just, starship, gh, docker, rg, fd, bat,
# delta, zellij, pueue, opencode.
#
# Tools handled elsewhere (don't double-up):
#   sesh, tv, worktrunk        → shell-startup mtime check
#   bw, marimo, thefuck, try   → cached eval at startup
#   mi-router                  → tyro self-gen at startup
#   fleet, mlf, pqsum, x       → hand-written eager-load
#
# Manual rerun (--force regenerates all even if cache fresh):
#   just completions-refresh
#   bash {{ .chezmoi.sourceDir }}/scripts/generate_completions.sh --force
#
# Skip this hook (cache files stay as they are):
#   export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1

set -e

[ "${CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN:-0}" = "1" ] && exit 0

generator="{{ .chezmoi.sourceDir }}/scripts/generate_completions.sh"
[ -x "$generator" ] || {
    echo "completions: generator not found at $generator (skipping)" >&2
    exit 0
}

bash "$generator" --quiet
```
</details></tool-use>

# Pitfalls

Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.

This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.

## Pitfalls vs the rest

This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:

| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |

A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.

## When to add a pitfall doc

Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:

- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)

## When NOT to add a pitfall doc

- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
  table below instead of duplicating
- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
  (cross-link only)
- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
  move on

## File template

See [`assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](#) in the
[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness),
or copy the structure of an existing entry below.

But there's a subtlety with how `set -e` interacts with AND-OR lists — it only triggers on the *last* command in the list. ```tmpl
#!/bin/bash
# Keep bat's compiled theme cache in sync with the managed Tokyo Night theme.
#
# `run_after_*`, NOT `run_onchange_after_*` (which is what this used to be).
# The cache lives OUTSIDE chezmoi's control (`~/.cache/bat/*.bin`, compiled from
# `~/.config/bat/themes/`) and is wiped or invalidated out-of-band by events that
# never touch the `.tmTheme` file, so its content hash is the wrong gate:
#
#   - `bat cache --clear` — the documented delta-crash recovery in
#     pitfalls/git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation.md
#   - this script's own delta health check below (it clears on incompatibility)
#   - a `~/.cache` wipe, or a $HOME restored/synced without `~/.cache`
#   - a `bat` upgrade: the cache is bincode keyed to the bat version that wrote
#     it, so the new bat ignores (and warns about) a cache from the old one
#
# Under the old onchange hash, none of those re-ran this script, so the cache
# stayed missing forever and EVERY `bat` invocation — including every fzf / tv /
# yazi preview that shells out to bat — printed:
#
#   [bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night', using default.
#
# See pitfalls/bat-theme-cache-cleared-never-rebuilt.md.
#
# Cost when the cache is already healthy: 2 `bat` invocations + 3 stat calls
# (~15 ms). The expensive `bat cache --build` only runs when something is
# actually stale.
#
# Skip this hook entirely (cache left exactly as-is):
#   export CHEZMOI_SKIP_BAT_CACHE=1

set -e

[ "${CHEZMOI_SKIP_BAT_CACHE:-0}" = "1" ] && exit 0

export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
fi
{{ else -}}
if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
fi
{{ end -}}

info() { echo -e "\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m $1"; }
success() { echo -e "\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m $1"; }
warn() { echo -e "\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m $1"; }

if ! command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Quiet: bat is optional, and this script now runs on every apply.
    exit 0
fi

CACHE_DIR="$(bat --cache-dir)"
THEME_FILE="$(bat --config-dir)/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme"
BAT_VERSION="$(bat --version | awk '{print $2}')"

if [[ ! -f "$THEME_FILE" ]]; then
    warn "bat theme file not found: $THEME_FILE"
    exit 0
fi

# Fast path — the compiled cache exists, was written by THIS bat version, and is
# newer than the theme source. Anything else falls through to a rebuild.
if [[ -f "$CACHE_DIR/themes.bin" ]] \
    && [[ ! "$THEME_FILE" -nt "$CACHE_DIR/themes.bin" ]] \
    && grep -qx "bat_version: $BAT_VERSION" "$CACHE_DIR/metadata.yaml" 2>/dev/null; then
    exit 0
fi

# A (bat, delta) pair already proven incompatible below stays cleared — without
# this stamp the script would rebuild → delta-check → clear on every single
# apply, forever. The stamp lives outside $CACHE_DIR because `bat cache --clear`
# removes that directory wholesale.
STAMP_DIR="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/chezmoi"
STAMP="$STAMP_DIR/bat-cache-delta-incompatible"
if command -v delta >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    DELTA_VERSION="$(delta --version | awk '{print $2}')"
else
    DELTA_VERSION="none"
fi
STAMP_KEY="bat=$BAT_VERSION delta=$DELTA_VERSION"

if [[ -f "$STAMP" ]] && [[ "$(cat "$STAMP")" == "$STAMP_KEY" ]]; then
    info "bat cache intentionally left empty: $STAMP_KEY is a known delta-incompatible pair"
    info "  (see pitfalls/git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation.md; rm $STAMP to retry)"
    exit 0
fi

info "Rebuilding bat theme cache (bat $BAT_VERSION)"
bat cache --build >/dev/null

# delta embeds its own bat; a cache written by an incompatible bat makes delta
# abort with a bogus multi-petabyte allocation. Verify on the rendering path —
# `delta --version` does NOT exercise it. Do not regress this to a version check.
if [[ "$DELTA_VERSION" != "none" ]] && ! printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "bat cache is incompatible with delta $DELTA_VERSION; clearing cache so git pager keeps working"
    bat cache --clear >/dev/null
    mkdir -p "$STAMP_DIR"
    printf '%s\n' "$STAMP_KEY" >"$STAMP"
    warn "BAT_THEME stays unset in the shell (dot_config/shell/25_bat.sh) — bat uses its own default"
    exit 0
fi
rm -f "$STAMP"

if bat --list-themes 2>/dev/null | grep -qx 'tokyonight_night'; then
    success "bat theme cache rebuilt (tokyonight_night available)"
else
    warn "bat cache rebuilt but 'tokyonight_night' is not listed — BAT_THEME will stay unset"
fi

```

```sh
# 25_bat.sh - bat configuration (shared by zsh/bash)

# Check if bat is installed
command -v bat &>/dev/null || return 0

# Tokyo Night theme. The `.tmTheme` source is managed by chezmoi at
# ~/.config/bat/themes/, and compiled into bat's binary cache by
# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl.
#
# BAT_THEME is exported ONLY when that compiled cache is actually present. bat
# prints
#   [bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night', using default.
# on EVERY invocation when the theme isn't compiled in — which means every fzf /
# tv / yazi preview and every `delta` render, one warning line each. The cache
# is legitimately absent in two cases: on a fresh box before the first
# `chezmoi apply`, and on hosts where the run-script deliberately cleared it
# because the installed bat/delta pair is incompatible (see
# pitfalls/git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation.md). Leaving BAT_THEME unset
# there makes bat fall back to its own default silently instead.
#
# See pitfalls/bat-theme-cache-cleared-never-rebuilt.md.
_bat_cache_dir="${BAT_CACHE_PATH:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/bat}"
_bat_theme_file="${BAT_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/bat}/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme"
if [ -f "$_bat_cache_dir/themes.bin" ] && [ -f "$_bat_theme_file" ]; then
    export BAT_THEME="tokyonight_night"
fi
unset _bat_cache_dir _bat_theme_file

```

```md
# `[bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night'` on every bat/delta call, forever

**Symptoms** (grep this section): `[bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night', using default.` printed on EVERY `bat` invocation and every `git diff` / `git show` render (delta embeds bat); the warning line leaks into fzf / `tv` / yazi previews that shell out to bat; `bat --list-themes | grep tokyonight` prints nothing; `ls "$(bat --cache-dir)"` says `No such file or directory`; `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` **is** present and chezmoi-managed; repeated `chezmoi apply` runs never fix it and print nothing about bat.
**First seen**: 2026-07
**Affects**: any host where `~/.cache/bat` was cleared or invalidated after the first successful apply — i.e. all of them, eventually.
**Status**: fixed (run-script converted from `run_onchange_after_` to a self-healing `run_after_`, plus a shell-side guard).

## Symptom

\```console
$ git diff
[bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night', using default.
...

$ bat --list-themes | grep -i tokyo
$ ls "$(bat --cache-dir)"
ls: /Users/david/.cache/bat: No such file or directory

$ ls ~/.config/bat/themes/
tokyonight_night.tmTheme          # the source IS there

$ chezmoi apply                   # …and this never fixes it
\```

The confusing part is that everything chezmoi owns looks correct. `chezmoi status`
is clean, the `.tmTheme` file is deployed, `BAT_THEME` is exported — and the warning
still fires on every single command that renders a diff.

Note the warning only appears on the **highlighting** path: with color off
(`bat file.md | cat`, or a non-tty without `--color=always`) bat never looks the
theme up, so a quick check can look deceptively healthy. Reproduce it with:

\```sh
BAT_THEME=tokyonight_night bat --color=always --style=plain --language=md <<< '# hi'
\```

## Root cause

Two independent things have to be true for a custom bat theme to work, and only
one of them is under chezmoi's control:

| Thing | Owner | Lives in |
|---|---|---|
| `tokyonight_night.tmTheme` source | chezmoi (`dot_config/bat/themes/`) | `~/.config/bat/themes/` |
| the **compiled** theme cache | `bat cache --build` | `~/.cache/bat/{themes,syntaxes}.bin` |

bat does *not* read `.tmTheme` files at runtime. It only reads the bincode cache,
which must be regenerated with `bat cache --build`.

The rebuild used to live in `run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl`, hash-gated
on the content of the `.tmTheme` file:

\```sh
# bat theme: {{ include "dot_config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme" | sha256sum }}
\```

That gate is wrong, because **the cache gets destroyed by events that never touch
the theme file**, so the hash never changes and the script never re-runs:

- `bat cache --clear` — the documented recovery for
  [`git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation`](git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation.md)
- the *same script's own* delta health check, which clears the cache when the
  installed bat/delta pair is incompatible — a guaranteed one-way trip under the
  old gate: cleared once, never rebuilt, even after the host got a compatible
  bat/delta later
- wiping `~/.cache`, or restoring/syncing a `$HOME` that excludes it
- upgrading `bat`: the cache is bincode keyed to the writing bat version
  (`~/.cache/bat/metadata.yaml` → `bat_version:`), so the new binary ignores a
  cache written by the old one

Once in that state, the only escape was to know to run `bat cache --build` by
hand. `chezmoi apply` — the thing you'd naturally reach for — was a no-op.

## Workaround

Immediate, on any host:

\```sh
bat cache --build
bat --list-themes | grep -qx tokyonight_night && echo ok
\```

## Prevention

Two fixes, both in this repo:

1. **`.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl`** (renamed from
   `run_onchange_after_25_…`) now runs on **every** apply and decides for itself
   whether a rebuild is needed. State outside chezmoi's control cannot be
   hash-gated on state inside it. Its fast path is 3 `bat` invocations + 2 stats
   (~150 ms) and rebuilds only when any of these fail:
   - `~/.cache/bat/themes.bin` exists
   - `metadata.yaml` records the *currently installed* bat version
   - `themes.bin` is not older than the `.tmTheme` source

   When the delta health check does clear the cache, the script writes a
   `bat=<ver> delta=<ver>` stamp to `~/.cache/chezmoi/bat-cache-delta-incompatible`
   so it doesn't rebuild-then-clear on every apply forever. Upgrading either tool
   changes the key and the pair is retried automatically.

2. **`dot_config/shell/25_bat.sh`** only exports `BAT_THEME` when the compiled
   cache *and* the `.tmTheme` file are both present. On a host that legitimately
   has no cache (fresh box before first apply, or a delta-incompatible pair), bat
   silently falls back to its own default instead of warning on every invocation.
   The pitfall above says "that warning is preferable to the crash" — it is, but
   not exporting the variable is better than both.

**Generalisable rule**: a `run_onchange_` hash is only valid when the *effect* of
the script lives somewhere chezmoi tracks. If the script's product is a cache, a
compiled artifact, or anything else outside the target-state tree, use `run_after_`
plus an explicit freshness check. Same reasoning as
`run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` (binary-mtime check for tools that
upgrade between applies).

## Related

- [`git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation.md`](git-delta-empty-stdin-huge-allocation.md)
  — the crash whose recovery (`bat cache --clear`) is one way to land here
- [`docs/tools/git_diff_workflow.md`](../docs/tools/git_diff_workflow.md) — the
  delta / diffnav / gh-dash stack that consumes the theme
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` — same
  "`run_after_` + explicit freshness check" shape, for the same class of reason

```

```text
111	## Config-wired previewers (EPUB · Kindle · dmg)
112	
113	Everything above except EPUB, Kindle e-books, and dmg is pure tool-install — yazi's built-ins handle
114	the routing. Those mimes aren't in yazi's built-in sets, so `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` wires them via
115	[`piper.yazi`](office-viewers.md#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism):
116	
117	```toml
118	{ url = "*.epub", run = 'piper -- pandoc -f epub -t plain "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
119	{ url = "*.mobi", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },  # + *.azw *.azw3 *.fb2
120	{ url = "*.dmg",  run = 'piper -- ( 7zz l "$1" 2>/dev/null || 7z l "$1" 2>/dev/null ) | head -n 200' },
121	```
122	
123	- **EPUB → full text** via pandoc (pandoc reads EPUB but not the Kindle formats).
124	- **Kindle `.mobi`/`.azw`/`.azw3`/`.fb2` → metadata** via [`view-ebook`](#kindle-e-books-calibre)
125	  (calibre `ebook-meta`). There's no fast headless way to render mobi/azw *text*, so the preview is a
126	  "book back-cover" (title / author / tags / description). Best-effort — nothing shows if calibre is absent.
127	- **dmg → file listing** via 7-Zip (`7zz`/`7z`).
128	- `2>/dev/null` is **load-bearing** — piper renders any stderr as an error preview.
129	- **No rule needed** for `.zip` / `.tar.*` / `.7z` / `.rar` or zip-based `.apk` / `.jar` / `.whl` /
130	  `.xpi` — yazi's built-in archive previewer lists them for free once 7-Zip is installed.
131	
132	### Kindle e-books (calibre) {#kindle-e-books-calibre}
133	
134	`view-ebook` (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-ebook`) resolves calibre's `ebook-meta` — on PATH,
135	else the macOS `/Applications/calibre.app` bundle, else the Linux prefix — and prints the book's
136	metadata (HTML-stripped, wrapped to the pane width). calibre isn't repo-managed by default; enable the
137	**`installCalibre`** init prompt to have the `devtools` role install it (brew cask on macOS, apt on
138	Linux). Already have calibre installed by hand? The preview just works, and the macOS cask install is
139	**skipped** when `/Applications/calibre.app` already exists (Homebrew won't install over an existing app,
140	and `--adopt` refuses on a version mismatch) — so the prompt only installs calibre where it's absent,
141	never touching a version you manage yourself. (EPUB stays on pandoc's full-text path, not view-ebook.)
142	
143	## Per-OS install
144	
145	| Tool | macOS (brew, `devtools`) | Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | Enables |
146	|---|---|---|---|
147	| **chafa** | `chafa` | apt `chafa` | image display fallback (all image-derived previews) |
148	| **poppler** | `poppler` | apt `poppler-utils` | PDF |
149	| **7-Zip** | `sevenzip` (`7zz`) | apt `p7zip-full` (`7z`) | archives + dmg |
150	| **resvg** | `resvg` | Linuxbrew → `cargo install resvg` (no apt pkg; non-fatal if absent) | SVG |
151	| ffmpeg | `ffmpeg` (`media_tools`, gated) | apt `ffmpeg` (gated) | video thumbnails |
152	| ImageMagick | `imagemagick` (`media_tools`, gated) | apt `imagemagick` (gated) | HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts |
153	| pandoc | `pandoc` (already in `devtools`) | apt `pandoc` | EPUB text |
154	| calibre (`ebook-meta`) | `calibre` cask — opt-in `installCalibre` | apt `calibre` — opt-in | Kindle .mobi/.azw/.azw3 metadata |
155	
156	## Gotchas
157	
158	- **Rename / shell popup with `rgb:…` junk on image hover** → the chafa OSC-query leak under
159	  tmux/zellij; fixed here by the `--probe off` shim — see [above](#chafa-probe-leak).
160	- **Ubuntu ImageMagick is v6.** apt ships ImageMagick 6 (no unified `magick`; weak HEIC), so HEIC/font
161	  previews may not work on Ubuntu even with `installMediaTools=true`. yazi wants **≥7.1.1**; v7 needs a
162	  PPA or source build (out of scope). macOS brew ImageMagick is v7 → fine.
163	- **Video/HEIC need `installMediaTools`.** ffmpeg + ImageMagick are opt-in. If mp4 thumbnails or HEIC
164	  previews are blank, re-run init with `installMediaTools=true` (or install ffmpeg/imagemagick by
165	  hand). Everything else in the baseline works without it.
166	- **resvg on Linux is best-effort.** No apt package → the role tries Linuxbrew then a one-time
167	  `cargo install resvg`. If neither is available, SVG simply previews as raw text — non-fatal.
168	- **Lowercase globs.** The `*.epub` / `*.dmg` / `*.mobi` rules match lowercase extensions; `Book.EPUB`
169	  won't fire (yazi's built-ins are mime-based and unaffected).
170	- **Kindle previews are metadata, not text.** `.mobi`/`.azw`/`.azw3` show the book's title / author /
171	  description (via calibre `ebook-meta`), not the prose — there's no fast headless mobi/azw text
172	  renderer. Needs calibre (the `installCalibre` prompt, or a manual install). EPUB gets full text (pandoc).
173	- **Image-only pptx → slide thumbnail.** A deck whose slides are full-page images has no text for
174	  markitdown to extract, so view-office renders the first embedded slide image with chafa instead of a
175	  list of `![](imageN)`. It's detected cheaply by peeking at the slide XML with 7-Zip. See
176	  [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md).
177	- **chafa is a fallback, not a downgrade to avoid.** ascii-art is the correct behavior in a
178	  non-graphics terminal — see [above](#which-terminal-gets-crisp-images-vs-ascii-art).
179	- **Large image → `Image size exceeds limit`.** yazi's decode bound (`[tasks] image_bound`), not the
180	  terminal; raised to `[30000, 30000]` here — see [above](#image-size-limit).
181	
182	## Where things live
183	
184	| Surface | Path |
185	|---|---|
186	| Baseline tool install (chafa/poppler/7zip/resvg) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
187	| chafa `--probe off` shim (fixes the rename/shell popup) | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_chafa` |
188	| Media tool install (ffmpeg/ImageMagick, gated) | `dot_ansible/roles/media_tools/tasks/main.yml` |
189	| calibre install (opt-in `installCalibre`) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
190	| EPUB / Kindle / dmg previewer rules | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin] prepend_previewers` |
191	| Kindle metadata dispatcher | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-ebook` (+ 56_view_ebook_completion.*) |
192	| pptx image-only thumbnail | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office` (`render_pptx`) |
193	| yazi install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (`# --- yazi ---`) |
194	| tmux image passthrough | `dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl` (`allow-passthrough on`) |
195

Never drop the shim or its `--probe off`; yazi hardcodes the bare `chafa` call so shadowing is the only lever. | [docs/tools/yazi-previews.md](docs/tools/yazi-previews.md) |

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-07-26 10:34:45Z)**_

兩個都修好了。

## 1. `.md` 沒有 pretty formatting

yazi 內建的 `code` previewer 只做 syntect 語法高亮 — 你看到的是**原始 markup**（`## Heading`、`**bold**`、`| a | b |`）。改成用已安裝的 `glow` 渲染：

```toml
{ url = "*.md",       run = 'piper -- glow -w "$w" -s "$t" "$1" 2>/dev/null || cat "$1"' },
{ url = "*.markdown", run = '…同上…' },
```

- `$w` = pane 寬度（glow 硬換行到剛好那寬度，resize 不會溢出/截斷表格）
- `$t` = yazi 自己偵測的 `dark`/`light`，顏色跟著終端走
- `|| cat` 讓沒有 glow release 的架構退回純文字，而不是空白 pane
- 捲動可用（piper 用 `job.skip` 重跑）；2.8 MB 的 md 最慢實測 ~160 ms

沒用 `Reledia/glow.yazi` plugin — 它寬度寫死 55、style 寫死 dark，還在用已棄用的 `ya.mgr_emit`/`ya.preview_widgets` API。piper 已經裝了，直接接更好。

想看原始碼就照舊 `Enter`/`o` 開 nvim。唯一美中不足：glow 會把連結目的地展開成絕對路徑印出來，link 密集的文件會有點吵。

## 2. `[bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night'`

根因不是主題檔，是**重建腳本的 gate 下錯了**。bat 執行期不讀 `.tmTheme`，只讀 `~/.cache/bat/*.bin`；而 `run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl` 的 hash 掛在 `.tmTheme` 上。你的 `~/.cache/bat` 整個不存在，但主題檔沒變 → 腳本永遠不再跑 → `chezmoi apply` 完全是 no-op。清掉 cache 的來源全都不碰主題檔：`bat cache --clear`（delta crash 的標準救援）、腳本自己的 delta guard、`~/.cache` 被清、bat 升級讓 bincode 失效。等於**清一次就永久壞掉**。

改法：

- 腳本改名成 `run_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl`，每次 apply 都自己檢查（themes.bin 在？`metadata.yaml` 的 bat 版本相符？比 `.tmTheme` 新？），只有過期才重建。健康時 ~150 ms（`brew shellenv` 只在 bat 不在 PATH 時才 eval）。
- delta guard 真的清 cache 時，寫一筆 `bat=<ver> delta=<ver>` 到 `~/.cache/chezmoi/bat-cache-delta-incompatible`，避免每次 apply 都「重建→清掉」無限循環；升級任一邊就自動重試。
- `dot_config/shell/25_bat.sh` 只在 cache 真的存在時才 `export BAT_THEME` — 沒有 cache 的機器靜默用 bat 預設，而不是每行都跳警告。

驗證（全部實跑過）：清空 cache → 腳本自癒重建；假 delta 失敗 → 寫 stamp、二次執行不重建；真 delta 回來 → 重建並清 stamp。症狀本身也重現確認：`BAT_THEME=tokyonight_night bat --color=always` 無 cache 時印警告，有 cache 時正確出 Tokyo Night 配色。**你這台已經修好了**（cache 已重建），新開的 shell 直接生效。

## 驗證與文件

`yazi --debug` 解析設定無誤、TOML 通過、shellcheck 通過、pre-commit 全綠、隔離沙箱確認 `run_after_` 每次 apply 都執行。

The reason it degrades to ANSI 16 instead of using truecolor is termenv's logic: when `CLICOLOR_FORCE` is set and the detected profile is `Ascii` (which happens for non-TTY), it returns plain ANSI instead of checking the `TERM` or `COLORTERM` environment variables. So even though my shell has `COLORTERM=truecolor` and `TERM=xterm-256color` set, the forced mode still caps out at 16 colors. ```text
# Backlog Research

Long-form research, design notes, and paused troubleshooting for items listed in
[`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md). One file per topic, named with a slug that matches
the TODO entry.

## Why this exists

`TODO.md` is the **index** — short titles with priority/effort tags. This folder
is the **knowledge base** — the actual investigation, options considered,
benchmarks, error messages, and decisions that informed the TODO entry. The goal
is **resume-friendliness**: when you (or an agent) come back to an item three
months later, the doc here lets you pick up in 5 minutes instead of re-running
30 minutes of investigation.

This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `backlog/**`) — it
is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.

## When to add a doc here

Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` file when **any** of these apply:

- The TODO item carries a `P?` tag (it requires evaluation; record what was tried)
- You did meaningful troubleshooting but didn't ship a fix (capture the trace
  before it evaporates)
- Multiple options were considered (record the trade-offs, not just the winner)
- An external blocker exists (waiting on upstream release, host availability)
- The implementation is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)

`[S]` items rarely need a doc unless there's surprising context.

## When NOT to add a doc here

- Item is `[S]` and obvious (e.g., "change a TOML key") — just put the file path
  in the TODO entry
- Already covered by a `docs/this_repo/*.md` or `docs/tools/*.md` page
  (cross-link instead, that's user-facing reference)
- Speculation only ("would be cool to...") with no investigation — keep it as a
  one-liner in `TODO.md` first; promote to a doc when you actually look into it

=== TODO format ===
30:- [ ] **[S] Starship status-aware modules** — enable `status` / `cmd_duration` / `shlvl` / `container` in `dot_config/starship.toml`. Pure additive, no risk. → [research](backlog/starship-context-modules.md)
31:- [ ] **[S] tmux2k bandwidth bug** — drop `bandwidth` from `@tmux2k-right-plugins` in `dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf` (uint64 underflow already documented in the file's own comment). → [research](backlog/tmux2k-tuning.md)

```md
# yazi Markdown preview: getting glow's native 256-colour output

**Status**: shipped a working 16-colour fix; the 256-colour upgrade is deferred.
**TODO tag**: `[S]` under `P3`.
**Ships today**: `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` → `{ url = "*.md", run = 'piper -- CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 glow -w "$w" -s "$t" "$1" 2>/dev/null || cat "$1"' }`

## Context

yazi previews `.md` through `piper.yazi` → `glow`. piper spawns the child with
`stdout(Command.PIPED)` — a pipe, never a pty. glow renders via
glamour → lipgloss → **termenv**, and termenv chooses its colour profile by
probing stdout:

| stdout | termenv profile | glow emits |
|---|---|---|
| pipe, no override | `Ascii` | `ESC[;;1m` — attributes only, **every colour component stripped** |
| pipe + `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` | `ANSI` (16 colours) | `ESC[37m`, `ESC[93;104;1m` |
| real pty | `ANSI256` | `ESC[38;5;252m`, `ESC[38;5;228;48;5;63;1m` |

That first row is the "formatted but monochrome" bug: structure renders (bold and
reverse survive) while the colour looks broken. `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` fixes it — and
is what upstream [`glow.yazi`](https://github.com/Reledia/glow.yazi) sets too.

## What was measured

Forcing termenv out of an `Ascii` detection lands on plain **ANSI-16**, never 256.
No environment tweak moves it — all of these produced byte-identical 16-colour output
on glow 2.1.1 / macOS:

\```sh
CLICOLOR_FORCE=1
CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 COLORTERM=truecolor
CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 TERM=xterm-256color COLORTERM=truecolor
CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 FORCE_COLOR=3 COLORTERM=truecolor
FORCE_COLOR=3                      # no effect at all — not a termenv variable
\```

Only a real pty reaches 256-colour (confirmed with `python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn([...])'`).

## Options for 256-colour

1. **`script(1)` wrapper** — the portable-ish pty allocator. Blocked on syntax
   divergence: BSD/macOS is `script -q /dev/null cmd args…`, util-linux wants
   `script -qec "cmd args…" /dev/null`. Encoding an OS switch inside a yazi
   previewer string (already single-quoted and containing `"$1"`) is nasty, and pty
   output carries `\r\n` so it needs a `| tr -d '\r'` that must not swallow piper's
   stderr contract.
2. **In-house `view-markdown` launcher** doing the pty allocation in Python. Clean,
   but per the repo contract a new `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` drags in two
   completion files, a `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` § F row and an aliases row —
   a lot of surface for a colour-depth nicety.
3. **Custom glamour style JSON** (`glow -s /path/to/style.json`) — does **not**
   help. Quantisation happens after style resolution, so a hand-tuned palette gets
   flattened to the same 16 colours.

## Why deferred

ANSI-16 is not obviously worse in this repo's setup: those 16 slots come from the
terminal's own palette, so the preview tracks the active Ghostty/tmux theme instead
of glow's hardcoded 256-colour ramp. The remaining gap is a subtle gradient
difference on headings and code spans. Revisit if glow ever grows a
`--color-profile` flag (which would collapse this to a one-token change), or if
option 2 becomes cheap because a `view-markdown` CLI is wanted for other reasons.

## Related

- [`docs/tools/yazi-previews.md` § Markdown](../docs/tools/yazi-previews.md) — the shipped behaviour
- `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin] prepend_previewers` — the rules themselves
- termenv's profile logic: `EnvColorProfile()` → forced-out-of-`Ascii` returns `ANSI`

```

```bash
git --no-pager diff --stat pitfalls/README.md && git add pitfalls/README.md && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(bat): self-heal the theme cache instead of hash-gating on the .tmTheme

`[bat warning]: Unknown theme 'tokyonight_night', using default.` fired on
every bat invocation and every `git diff` (delta embeds bat), with no way to
recover via `chezmoi apply`.

bat never reads `.tmTheme` at runtime — only the bincode cache under
`~/.cache/bat`, which lives outside chezmoi's target-state tree. The rebuild
script was `run_onchange_` hashed on the theme file, so every event that wipes
that cache without touching the theme (`bat cache --clear` — the documented
delta-crash recovery, the script's own delta guard, a `~/.cache` wipe, a bat
upgrade invalidating the bincode format) left the cache missing permanently.
Clearing it once was a one-way trip.

- rename to `run_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl`: runs every apply, decides for
  itself via themes.bin presence + `metadata.yaml` bat version + mtime vs the
  theme source. Fast path ~150ms; `brew shellenv` only evaluated when bat isn't
  already on PATH.
- record the offending `bat=<ver> delta=<ver>` pair in
  `~/.cache/chezmoi/bat-cache-delta-incompatible` when the delta health check
  clears the cache, so it can't rebuild-then-clear on every apply forever.
  Upgrading either tool changes the key and retries automatically.
- `25_bat.sh` exports BAT_THEME only when the compiled cache exists, so a
  cache-less host is silent rather than warning on every rendered line.
- add `CHEZMOI_SKIP_BAT_CACHE=1` escape hatch.

Verified end to end: cleared cache self-heals; a stubbed failing delta writes
the stamp and the next run skips the rebuild; restoring a working delta
rebuilds and clears the stamp. Symptom reproduced and confirmed gone via
`BAT_THEME=tokyonight_night bat --color=always`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git --no-pager log --oneline -1
```

Commit the yazi markdown preview feature

```bash
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(yazi): render Markdown previews with glow instead of raw source

yazi's built-in `code` previewer only syntax-highlights `.md` as source, so
hovering a README showed `## Heading` / `**bold**` / raw table pipes. Route
`*.md` and `*.markdown` through piper → glow so headings, emphasis, lists,
tables and fenced code blocks render as styled text.

    { url = "*.md", run = 'piper -- CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 glow -w "$w" -s "$t" "$1" 2>/dev/null || cat "$1"' }

Every piece is load-bearing:
- `$w` — pane width; glow hard-wraps to exactly that, so resizing never
  overflows or truncates a table mid-row.
- `$t` — piper's `dark`/`light` from yazi's own terminal detection, instead of
  pinning a palette.
- `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` — piper hands the child a pipe, so glow's termenv probe
  returns the `Ascii` profile and emits attribute-only escapes (`ESC[;;1m`):
  bold survives, every colour component is stripped, giving a formatted but
  monochrome preview. Forcing it restores colour, capped at ANSI-16 (no
  TERM/COLORTERM/FORCE_COLOR combination reaches 256 — only a real pty does;
  trade-offs in backlog/yazi-markdown-preview-truecolor.md).
- `|| cat` — plain-text preview rather than an empty pane on architectures
  where the devtools role skipped glow.

Not using the upstream Reledia/glow.yazi plugin: it hardcodes width 55 and a
dark style, and calls the deprecated ya.mgr_emit / ya.preview_widgets APIs.
piper is already installed and wired here.

Config validated with `yazi --debug`; worst-case render measured at ~160ms on
a 2.8MB markdown file, so scrolling stays responsive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git --no-pager log --oneline -2
```

53	## PATH augmentation
54	
55	Like [`fleet pueue`](pueue.md), this command prepends a fixed PATH prelude
56	on every host so user-installed binaries are visible to the
57	non-interactive SSH shell:
58	
59	```
60	~/.dotfiles/bin → ~/.cargo/bin → ~/.local/bin → ~/bin →
61	/opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin → /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin →
62	~/.linuxbrew/bin → $PATH
63	```
64	
65	Order favours package-manager dirs (`~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`) over
66	legacy `~/bin` so a stale download in `~/bin` doesn't shadow a fresher
67	`cargo install` of the same tool. `--no-augment-path` skips the prelude;
68	`--login` bypasses it (login shells load PATH from rc files instead).
69	
70	This is a known divergence from your interactive shell's PATH order — see
71	[pueue.md § PATH augmentation](pueue.md) for the full rationale.
72	
73	## AI summary mode

139	## Cache
140	
141	`scan` caches to `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/appsrc/<hostname>.json`, keyed
142	**per item by mtime** — a re-scan only recomputes apps whose bundle changed. The
143	forward-inventory calls (cheap) always re-run. Flags: `-r/--refresh` (recompute
144	all), `--no-cache` (don't read or write). Ballpark on a laptop: full GUI+CLI
145	scan ~15 s cold, ~5 s warm (~2 200 items); `which` is instant.
146	
147	## Integration
148	
149	- **`appsrc tui`** — interactive Textual dashboard over the full inventory. A
150	  background worker scans (fast, no sizes); `/` filters by name/source, `s` sizes
151	  the currently-visible rows and sorts biggest-first (bounding `du` cost to what's
152	  on screen), `o`/`n` sort by source/name, `Enter` opens the size breakdown,
153	  `t`/`m` show the selected tool's `tldr`/`man` page (suspends into the pager),
154	  `y`/`r` copy path / reveal, `R` rescan, `q` quits. Needs a real terminal.
155	- **`tv appsrc`** — fuzzy-pick the full GUI+CLI inventory; type a source label
156	  (`cask`, `manual`, `app-store`, `apt`…) to narrow. `Enter` = detail, `Alt+S` =
157	  size, `Alt+T`/`Alt+M` = tldr/man, `Alt+C` = copy path, `Alt+O` = reveal,
158	  `Alt+J` = JSON.
159	- **`tv appsrc-size`** — the same picker pre-sorted by footprint (biggest first,
160	  human sizes shown) for hunting space hogs; preview/`Enter` = the size report.
161	- **Completions** shell out to `appsrc scan --list-names` for GUI app names + PATH
162	  commands, so `appsrc which/size <Tab>` completes either.
163	
164	`appsrc` is the *runtime* companion to
165	[`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`](../this_repo/tool-managers.md), which records
166	how **this repo** installs tools by design; `appsrc` inspects whatever is
167	actually on the machine.

### Provider routing: OpenRouter / Ollama

The `http` agent talks an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint directly via `curl` + `jq` — no agent CLI required. The same code path handles **OpenRouter free models** (Bearer key) and **local Ollama** (no auth) since both speak the same schema. `http` is never auto-detected; opt in with `AICAP_AGENT=http` or `-a http`.

```sh
# OpenRouter — free Gemini Flash, ~5s round-trip, requires a (free) account
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...
export AICAP_AGENT=http
# defaults already point at OpenRouter + Gemini Flash free; no other vars needed
aifix
# Switch model:
AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free aifix

# Ollama — fully offline / privacy-sensitive
ollama serve &                          # or `brew services start ollama`
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
export AICAP_AGENT=http
export AICAP_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions
export AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b
aifix
```

74	## Chezmoi templating conventions
75	
76	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
77	
78	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
79	
80	| Predicate | Use |
81	|---|---|
82	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
83	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
84	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
85	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
86	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
87	
88	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).

90	## Hard repo invariants
91	
92	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
93	
94	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
95	
96	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
97	
98	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
99	
100	**Hard rules**:
101	
102	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
103	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
104	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
105	
106	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
107	
108	### Three-tier user-local override layer
109	
110	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
111	
112	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
113	
114	```
115	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
116	```
117	
118	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
119	
120	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
121	
122	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
123	
124	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
125	
126	**Hard rules**:
127	
128	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
129	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
130	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
131	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
132	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
133	
134	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
135	
136	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.

146	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
147	
148	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
149	
150	**Hard rules**:
151	
152	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
153	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
154	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
155	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
156	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. 157

159	
160	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
161	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
162	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
163	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.

169	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
170	
171	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
172	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
173	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
174	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
175	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
176	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
177	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
178	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
179	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
180	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
181	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.

183	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
184	
185	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (tomlkit overlay — managed tables enforced, herdr's runtime writeback preserved), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
186	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
187	
188	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).

191	
192	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
193	
194	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
195	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
196	
197	**Hard rules**:
198	
199	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
200	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
201	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
202	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
203	
204	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
205	
206	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
207	
208	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
209	
210	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
211	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
212	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
213	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
214	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
215	
216	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
217	
218	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
219	
220	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
221
```
</details></tool-use>

48:## Load order
--- chezmoi-templating decision table? ---
3:A short guide to deciding which knob to branch on in a chezmoi template: `.profile` (a user role we prompt for at init), `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` (auto-detected facts), `.chezmoi.hostname` (per-machine overrides), or an env var like `WORK_MACHINE` (per-session).
20:| `.chezmoi.arch` | What CPU arch? | Auto-detected (`runtime.GOARCH`) | `amd64`, `arm64`, `arm`, `386`, … | Binary availability (Apple Silicon-only casks, armv7l fallbacks) |
32:Anti-pattern: adding a `.profile` value to encode a distinction chezmoi already knows. The historical example in this repo was `macos_intel` (= darwin + amd64), which forced every macOS-specific branch to become `or (eq .profile "macos") (eq .profile "macos_intel")` because most macOS logic is the same on both architectures. The fix is two cheap built-ins: `.chezmoi.os` for the OS-wide branches, `.chezmoi.arch` for the small number of arm64-only binaries.
49:{{ if and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64") -}}
50:cask "chatgpt"  # arm64-only release
54:Inside a file that is only consumed on macOS anyway (e.g. `Brewfile.darwin`), the `.chezmoi.os` part is redundant — `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` alone is enough.
```

三個 commit 都進去了，你原本的 raycast 那批未提交檔案我完全沒碰。

## 顏色問題的真正原因

不是主題、不是 `-s` 參數 — 是 **glow 偵測不到 TTY**。

glow → glamour → lipgloss → **termenv**，而 termenv 是靠探測 stdout 決定 color profile。piper 給 child 的是 **pipe 不是 pty**，探測結果就是 `Ascii` profile，glow 於是只發「屬性碼」：`ESC[;;1m`（bold/reverse 留著，顏色分量全被剝掉）。所以你看到的正是**排版正常、顏色全無**。

修法一個 token：

```toml
{ url = "*.md", run = 'piper -- CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 glow -w "$w" -s "$t" "$1" 2>/dev/null || cat "$1"' }
```

已經 apply 到 `~/.config/yazi/yazi.toml` 並用 `yazi --debug` 驗過解析。

一個要先講的限制：termenv 被「強制脫離 `Ascii`」時只會退到 **ANSI-16**，不是 256。我把組合都試過了 —— `COLORTERM=truecolor`、`TERM=xterm-256color`、`FORCE_COLOR=3` 全部無效，輸出 byte 相同；只有真 pty 才拿得到 256 色（用 `python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn(...)'` 驗證過）。

好消息是 16 色是從**你終端自己的 palette** 取的，所以預覽會跟著 Ghostty/tmux 主題走，不是 glow 寫死的色階。要 256 色得包 pty：`script(1)` 語法 BSD 跟 util-linux 不相容（`script -q /dev/null cmd` vs `script -qec "cmd" /dev/null`），而且 pty 輸出帶 `\r\n` 要再 `tr -d '\r'`，塞進 previewer 字串太髒；另一條是開新的 `view-markdown` launcher，但按 repo 規約會連帶兩個 completion 檔 + 兩張表的 row，為了色深不划算。分析寫進 `backlog/yazi-markdown-preview-truecolor.md`，TODO 掛 P3 `[S]`。
